styles.name: Acid Graphics
styles.coreTrick: The primary is pushed to full chroma and paired with a computed fluorescent clash colour at near-equal luminance, then every display line is individually warped (stretched on a wave, compressed, outlined with echoes) over a hidden 12-column grid.
styles.colourRecipe: Primary re-printed at 100% saturation with lightness by hue band; a muted primary (s<24) falls back to fixed #B6FF00. The clash is chartreuse beside a dark acid, hot magenta beside a green/yellow one, else the hue 165 degrees round at equal luminance. Soft accent replaced by fixed lime. Canvas near-black (L 2.4) or near-white.

remainder.what: OKLCH clash search (gamut bisection, luminance solve, dull-hue rejection, fallback offsets)
remainder.whyCode: iterative colour search over gamut; no closed form a token or CSS can express

remainder.what: Per-letter warped headline with wave, compressed middle line and fit-to-column sizing
remainder.whyCode: per-letter layout computed from line length and index

remainder.what: The flyer: composed 4:5 HTML poster (name, slogan, info grid, stub, kana spine, sponsor wall) with two SVG displacement filters
remainder.whyCode: bespoke composition and hand-drawn marks; only the filters and ripple are generator-shaped

remainder.what: Luminance-delta readout and pair legend printed in the palette strip
remainder.whyCode: values computed at render time and injected through content:var()

remainder.what: Line-up bill type list and per-section info strip copy
remainder.whyCode: hand-authored layout and per-section strings

styles.notes: Light mode turns the hero into a full-bleed acid field (css 65-68). The file also holds a classic copy of the kit block (css 388-452) which was ignored.

styles.name: ASCII Art
styles.coreTrick: Everything is a character: colour is snapped to the 16 ANSI colours, the headline is built from a 5x7 bitmap as block glyphs, and the hero is the brand word rasterised on a canvas then mapped to a 70-step glyph ramp with line-ASCII edges.
styles.colourRecipe: Primary, secondary and accent each snap to the nearest ANSI colour by hue (dark 7 on paper, bright twins on black); a grey or near-grey uses weighted RGB distance. Exact client hex only appears in 0xRRGGBB readouts. Canvas pure #000 or paper #F4F1E8.

remainder.what: Canvas rasterisation of the brand word to a luminance grid and glyph-ramp mapping with edge detection
remainder.whyCode: image processing at render time, needs canvas and font loading

remainder.what: Bitmap-font block-letter headline builder with shadow and half-block variant
remainder.whyCode: per-pixel layout from a font table

remainder.what: Hue-aware ANSI snap and distinct-entry assignment
remainder.whyCode: nearest-colour search with exclusion

remainder.what: Live ticker re-rendering panels and re-rasterising on font load
remainder.whyCode: timer-driven DOM updates

remainder.what: Mono face selection with measured advance table so the glyph grid aligns
remainder.whyCode: grid maths depends on a known character advance per face

remainder.what: Readout hex as 0xRRGGBB through a token
remainder.whyCode: CSS cannot strip # from text

styles.notes: Most visible things (headline, hero, swatch glyph content) are code-built; the kit section is almost entirely css-recipe and reusable. The file also carries a classic copy of kit rules (css 359-364).

styles.name: Aurora Noir
styles.coreTrick: Every surface is an alpha of the ink colour on a near-black canvas (hairline fill, 1px lit top edge), lit by a soft colour-cloud wash, a conic beam and a hairline horizon arc above and below an opaque product-window mock.
styles.colourRecipe: Canvas capped at L 8% (dark). Primary is reserved for state (focus, switch, progress, status dot) and as the first beam and cloud colour; secondary is the second beam and cloud colour; accent is a small badge/dot and one headline word, shaded for contrast. The main action is ink-filled.

remainder.what: Product-window markup with sidebar, properties and activity rows from editable copy
remainder.whyCode: bespoke HTML with data-bound copy and brand-prefixed IDs

remainder.what: Issues table panel built by rewriting the shared list markup and computing the average
remainder.whyCode: transforms the framework's list output

remainder.what: Muted-text contrast loops against ink fills, per mode
remainder.whyCode: iterative contrast search

remainder.what: Export workarounds for html2canvas (beam, arc, grid fade, lit top edge box-shadow)
remainder.whyCode: renderer-specific overrides

remainder.what: anPrefix: issue-ID prefix from brand words
remainder.whyCode: text rule on the brand name

styles.notes: Almost all values are tokens or css-recipe; the weight is in the hero art. appSafe: the aurora and window are board-only; the kit keeps the hairline and lit-edge language. The file also holds a classic copy of kit rules.

styles.name: Bauhaus Poster
styles.coreTrick: Flat geometry only: a hard-edged 3x3 tile of quarter circles, semicircles and discs in the client primary plus two fixed poster pigments, with every control either square or fully round, 2px ink borders, and a huge tight lowercase headline.
styles.colourRecipe: Blue is always the client primary; red #EE4035 and yellow #F6C90E are fixed decorative planes (art, diagonal bar, card stripe). Secondary and accent run large only inside the art; in the UI they stay small tags and one highlight plane.

remainder.what: Hand-composed 3x3 cell table with the overlapping circle and triangle that overflow the box
remainder.whyCode: composition is authored, not derived; a generator could take it as a table but a good default needs design

remainder.what: Diagonal bar and thin ink bar angled to 21 degrees, placed behind the art
remainder.whyCode: hand-tuned positions and angles relative to the hero

remainder.what: Highlight word clipped with a hard-stop gradient that flips colour at 46%
remainder.whyCode: background-clip text trick that is fragile on dark canvases

styles.notes: The simplest style: only the art is svg-generator, the rest is css-recipe. It has no tokens() beyond the two fixed pigments and no canvas/headline hooks.

styles.name: Bento Grid
styles.coreTrick: The whole board is a 12-column grid of rounded tiles on a slightly darker canvas, with one radius, one gap, no borders, one solid primary action tile, secondary-tinted tiles and huge stat numerals.
styles.colourRecipe: Canvas a step darker than the tile (light mode); the tile is white mixed with canvas. The primary fills exactly one action tile, the lead numeral and the product mock; secondary tints the stage and the lead stat tile; accent is one dot. Muted and primary text are walked toward ink until they pass on the tile.

remainder.what: Phone product mock with floating chips and cropped rise
remainder.whyCode: bespoke HTML with editable copy

remainder.what: Deck Patterns stage as a bento of pattern images with fixed tile sizes
remainder.whyCode: deck hook placing pattern images at computed slot sizes

remainder.what: Deck In-product and Material bentos
remainder.whyCode: deck slides built from the board copy

remainder.what: Squeeze-and-lift transform pairs across kit components
remainder.whyCode: one rule per component, not parameterisable by one number

styles.notes: The JS holds no look-defining logic; the look is CSS plus tokens. The shadow tokens (--ab-shadow, js 120-125) are defined but the tile CSS sets box-shadow none (css 34), so the 'one soft shadow' in the header comment is stale. The file also holds a classic copy of the app block (css 441-470).

notes: Schema fit: moves carry no per-style numeric values (the same move holds different numbers per style), so those live in usedBy.variant text only. 'category' has no value for palette-chip shapes or hero composition, so those were filed under structure. Kit moves are tagged by component in kitScope; board-only moves have an empty kitScope and appSafe false. Seed ids unused: mono-plus-accent, duotone-ink, tonal-ramp, stretched-display, mixed-face-headline, glossy-single-action, clear-glass-panel, grain-overlay, halftone-dots. soft-raised-relief not used: bento shadow tokens exist but tile CSS sets none. contrast-lift is a generic helper the framework could provide as a built-in rather than a per-style move. The seed 'ink-filled-selected' was widened to cover other fills via the fill param. Classic copies of rules inside each css file were ignored as instructed. Line ranges are from reads of the files; kit ranges cite the section headers and signature comment blocks.
